hero.title: Eight devices in build, three concluded
hero.text: Each project starts with a person, a patient group or a clinician's referral. Every device goes to its user at no cost, and the designs stay open source.
hero.imageAlt: Y-AID students building the wheelchair scale prototype

currentIntro.title: The 2026–27 projects
currentIntro.text: Want to work on one? [Write to the president](contact.html#join) with your year, your major and the project that caught your eye.

current.name: Northern
current.description: An affordable device that makes range-of-motion practice more engaging, at home or in outpatient care, within the guidance of a person’s therapist.
current.imageAlt: A white 3D-printed arm and hand frame with tendon strings

current.name: Hospital button
current.description: A textured silicone overlay in a 3D-printed frame, with indentations that guide the thumb so patients recovering from stroke can work a hospital remote.
current.imageAlt: A hospital bedside remote with large labelled buttons

current.name: Hospital urinal
current.description: Simple attachments for standard hospital urinals that reduce spills and improve the handle, with no need to replace existing equipment.
current.imageAlt: An empty adjustable hospital bed in a patient room

current.name: Adjustable prosthetic
current.description: An open-source, modular, 3D-printed arm that adjusts as a child grows, so single parts can be replaced instead of the whole device.
current.imageAlt: A blue 3D-printed prosthetic hand with string tendons

current.name: Seated support after stroke
current.description: An alert that tells nurses when a patient begins to slip from their chair, plus a non-restrictive way to keep them seated safely.
current.imageAlt: A microcontroller board wired to a distance sensor on a breadboard

current.name: Rehabilitation bike
current.description: An accessible exercise bike that trains arms and legs together, with adjustable resistance, for people rebuilding strength after stroke.
current.imageAlt: An arm-and-leg exercise bike frame in a lab

current.name: Wheelchair scale
current.description: A portable, lower-cost scale that lets people weigh themselves without transferring out of their wheelchair.
current.imageAlt: A wheelchair user beside the team’s scale prototype

current.name: Rehabilitation glove
current.description: A comfortable, low-cost robotic silicone glove that helps people practise gripping and everyday hand movements after stroke.
current.imageAlt: A printed rehabilitation glove prototype worn on a hand

pastIntro.title: Three concluded projects
pastIntro.text: Each began with a single person's goal and shaped how the club designs today.

past.name: ForkLift
past.description: A button-controlled arm support that lifts the forearm, so a person with Duchenne muscular dystrophy can eat on their own.
past.imageAlt: A young wheelchair user trying the ForkLift arm support at a table

past.name: Elbow-controlled prosthetic
past.description: A functional arm for a young Yale New Haven Hospital patient, with a detachable piece for basketball and silverware.
past.imageAlt: A child holding up an orange 3D-printed prosthetic arm

past.name: The cello arm
past.description: A free 3D-printed arm that helped an 11-year-old cellist place her bow, later paired with a mobile app.
past.imageAlt: A printed prosthetic arm holding a cello bow on the strings
